Subject: Onboarding: model shortlist + operational assumptions

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To get the onboarding work scheduled with Engineering and CS, we put together an initial model shortlist and a few operational assumptions that will drive capacity and configuration. I attached a CSV with the shortlist and a short notes column (attachment: model_shortlist.csv).

Could you confirm the items below so we can finalize the mutual action plan:
- Primary inference endpoints you plan to use (chat/summarization, semantic search, rerank).
- Typical and upper-bound context length (avg tokens, 95th percentile).
- Expected query volume: MAU and avg queries per MAU, plus peak multiplier during campaigns.
- Latency SLOs (p95 target) and whether you prefer latency or unit-cost optimization.
- Any constraints on data residency or private deployment (VPC/on-prem).

If you can reply with those points, we’ll map to cost/latency profiles and propose a two-path implementation (cost-optimized + latency-critical) with recommended models, batching, and cache strategy. Proposed internal kickoff window: week of May 10.

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmeanalytics.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: model shortlist + operational assumptions

Connor —

Great to get this moving. Answers below and I attached a usage snapshot for Q1 to give historical context.

- Primary endpoints: 1) synchronous user chat (summarization + follow-up Q/A) 2) batch semantic search for recommendations, 3) light reranking for top-10 results.
- Context length: typical chat context ~1,200 tokens (user message + 2 doc excerpts). 95th percentile for deep dives ~8,000 tokens (some legal/finance docs).
- Volume: ~25,000 MAU; avg 3 queries per MAU/day → ~75k queries/day baseline. Peak multiplier: up to 8x during monthly reporting windows and product launches.
- Latency SLOs: chat p95 <= 400ms ideally; search can tolerate up to 1s p95. If forced to choose: prioritize chat latency.
- Data residency: US only for now, no on-prem requirement at launch.

We can share a small sample of anonymized request traces if that helps sizing. Attached: usage_snapshot_q1.pdf.

—Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Product, Acme Analytics
samantha@acmeanalytics.com
[Attachment: usage_snapshot_q1.pdf (application/pdf)]

On Thu, Apr 29, 2027 at 11:03 AM Samantha Lee <samantha@acmeanalytics.com> wrote:
> - Context length: typical chat context ~1,200 tokens (user message + 2 doc excerpts). 95th percentile for deep dives ~8,000 tokens (some legal/finance docs).

Thanks for the details, Samantha — this clarifies a few hard constraints. Based on the volume/latency mix you described, here is a recommended operational approach (high level):

1) Model shortlist (attached as CSV earlier) — condensed recommendations here:
   - Redwave-70B-q4f (primary for long-context, high-quality summarization) — use for heavy deep-dive threads and batch search re-ranking where quality is critical.
   - Llama2-13B-8bit (low-latency chat path) — optimized for p95 <= 400ms with small context windows and prefix/KV cache.
   - Redwave-7B-int8 (cost-optimized fallback) — for low-cost routing on high-volume, low-complexity queries.

2) Routing & caching strategy:
   - Route by intent: user-chat -> Llama2-13B unless prompt triggers long-context -> Redwave-70B.
   - Prefix/KV cache for repeated context chunks (legal doc intros, template text) to reduce tokenization & compute for repeated requests.
   - Short-circuit rerank to a smaller candidate set and call Redwave-70B only for final top-3.

3) Token-volume estimates (baseline -> peak):
   - Baseline queries/day: 75k. Avg tokens/query (chat): 1,800 tokens (prompt+response) -> 135M tokens/day.
   - 95th percentile deep-dive fraction: 3% of queries -> 2.25k calls/day at ~12k tokens -> ~27M tokens/day.
   - Peak multiplier x8 -> up to ~1.1B tokens/day across both paths.

4) Infrastructure and cost levers:
   - Consider dedicated capacity (Reserved) for the chat low-latency pool to guarantee p95 targets during peaks.
   - Enable autoscale with burst capacity for Redwave-70B to avoid queuing on deep dives.
   - Quantization + batching recommendations are in ops_estimates.xlsx (attached).

Next asks: can you confirm whether you want a single rollout (both paths live) or a staged rollout (chat first, search/rerank after)? Also please confirm if sampling for quality monitoring (we'll keep 0.5% of calls for eval hooks) is acceptable.

Attachment: ops_estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet with capacity scenarios and cost projections)

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
